I've kept a tight lip all summer, but now it's over.
Last April I crossed paths with the wrong southern Colorado State Patrol officer during the last blizzard on Wolfcreek Pass. Long story short, he ended up writing me a ticket for $1200.

After 3 trips to Creed Colorado this summer I finally couldn't ask for a better outcome. Yes it costed me 850 dollars per trip, although it really didn't cost me that much because I used my vacation pay each time, but I would have rather actually went on a vacation. 100 for fuel, 200 for motel, and 2 days off work for every trip.

Let me back up a few years. I've always known the Southern Colorado State Patrol is Rouge. I grew up in Durango and my friends and me traveling to Denver always got a speeding ticket whether we where speeding or not. Because of that we flew quite a bit, as it was faster and cheaper if you drove a shiny car. That being said, this time I had to do what's right and fight for it.

All summer I have been sweating this hanging over my head, sometimes mad at the world and in a horrible slump. How dare they pick on me having driven every mountain pass in Colorado in all kinds of weather, and specifically over a thousand trips over Wolfcreek, Coalbank, Molas, Redmountain, Vail, and Eisenhower. It's a real slap in the face to end this way now. 

I woke up in a hotel room Friday morning with an unexplained peace about the day, something just told me to swallow my pride and go with the flow. I started the proceedings with.....

I totally agree with the Colorado Chain Laws, I drive Colorado state owned buses five days a week between Denver and Grand Junction, the problem is we have a never ending supply of drivers who never seen snow before. But I assure you that I am not the guy that this law is meant to target. I presented my evidence, three different printouts of the Colorado chain laws, and pictures of Chainlaw signs, charter buses, state buses, and the cotrip screenshots that said passenger traction law but nothing about CMV chainlaw. I also submitted the dashcam videos of the incident. 

Much to my surprise the judge allowed me to run to my pickup for my laptop, plugged it in, and narrated the video. The Judge had me pause the video to explain what Autochains are and how they work. At the crux of my defense was the fact that the officer told me twice, because I questioned it, that Autochains are not legal in Colorado, but they are, and specifically on buses because the use of regular tire chains scratch the side of the bus with clearance issues. After that the officer started explaining his side of the story, with his lapel video. He also disagreed with me saying he said Autochains where not legal in Colorado, and that he told me to drop what I was doing because I was going to get a big ticket. As his video went on he stopped, paused his video, looked at me then the Judge, he then said, The Colorado State Patrol would like to dismiss this case. I assume he realized that his video had better audio than mine and would prove that he said Autochains where not legal in Colorado. 

After the equipment was shutoff the Judge and the officer both thanked me for teaching them something. Then the officer walked up to me and apologized and held his hand out for a shake. I said absolutely, you where doing your job, no hard feelings. And I honestly feel that way.
